summary:
AgriSense is designed as a web-based agricultural decision-support system using Python and Streamlit. It integrates NASA GLDAS soil-texture data, NASA POWER historical climate records, and FAO ECOCROP crop requirements. Users select a location on an interactive map of Pakistan, allowing the system to analyze environmental conditions and recommend potentially compatible crops through a transparent, rule-based ranking approach.

Traditional farming often relies on familiar crops and inherited agricultural practices, potentially overlooking other suitable options. AgriSense addresses this challenge by transforming complex environmental datasets into understandable crop recommendations. It also allows users to compare two geographical locations, explore seasonal conditions, and understand why particular crops are recommended.

AgriSense aims to make scientific agricultural information accessible to farmers, particularly those with limited access to soil analysis and agricultural expertise. By connecting NASA Earth data with practical crop guidance, the project encourages informed decision-making, exploration of alternative crops, and greater awareness of local environmental conditions. It demonstrates how space-based and environmental data can support more sustainable agricultural planning.
details:
AgriSense – NASA-Powered Smart Crop Recommendation System

Project Overview

AgriSense is a proposed web-based agricultural decision-support system designed to help farmers in Pakistan explore crop-growing opportunities beyond traditional farming practices. Many farmers repeatedly cultivate familiar crops without knowing whether their land and environmental conditions could support other agricultural options. AgriSense aims to bridge this information gap by transforming scientific environmental datasets into understandable, location-specific crop recommendations.

How It Works

The system features an interactive map of Pakistan where users can select any geographical location. The application automatically captures its latitude and longitude and retrieves relevant environmental information.

AgriSense integrates three major datasets:

  1. NASA GLDAS: Provides estimated soil-texture classifications for selected locations.
  2. NASA POWER: Supplies historical temperature and rainfall records to assess local climate patterns.
  3. FAO ECOCROP: Provides crop-specific environmental requirements, including soil preferences, temperature ranges, and rainfall needs.

A Python-based recommendation engine compares these environmental conditions with crop requirements to identify and rank potentially compatible crops. Users can also select two locations to compare their environmental characteristics and crop-growing potential.

Technologies and Development

AgriSense is designed using Python, Streamlit, Folium, Pandas, Xarray, and NASA POWER API integration. Streamlit provides the web interface, Folium supports interactive geographical selection, and Python handles dataset processing and crop compatibility analysis.

The system uses a transparent, rule-based recommendation approach, enabling users to understand why particular crops are suggested rather than receiving unexplained results.

Creativity and Innovation

AgriSense combines NASA environmental data with agricultural knowledge in a simple, interactive platform. Its distinctive features include location-based soil analysis, historical climate evaluation, explainable crop recommendations, seasonal exploration, and side-by-side geographical comparisons.
